newsitem.title: JORDAN: Iraqi group says Uday attacked with guns, grenades.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi group says Uday attacked with guns, grenades.

text.p: A Jordanian-based Iraqi opposition group spokesman said on Friday three to four attackers, hurling hand grenades and firing machine guns, attacked President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday on Thursday night.

Haroun Mohammad of the Iraqi National Accord (INA) told Reuters that eyewitnesses had said the windscreen of Uday's armoured car had been shattered in the attack in Baghdad's smart al-Mansour district.

Official Iraqi media in Baghdad quoted the presidential office as saying that Uday had been shot and wounded while driving through al-Mansour district on Thursday evening. They said he was taken to hospital but his condition "was not a matter of concern". The reports gave no details of the attack.
Mohammad said there were conflicting accounts of the attack. But he said eyewitnesses reported that Uday, 32, was travelling in a convoy of four cars when the gunmen struck.

"He was exposed to an attack by three or four masked people," Mohammad said. "The attack was characterised by attacks by hand grenade and machinegun. Eyewitnesses saw Uday's armoured car and windscreen had been been shattered."
Mohammad did not say who carried out the attack.
